clue.text: Desire hot instead of cold 7 soup

indicators.note: a soup is a jumble of ingredients, so the letters are stirred into a new order
says one letter takes the place of another within the word

parts.note: the answer to clue 7 across is the word to work on
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A craving for something hot rather than the chilled soup from another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of' swaps one C of RECYCLE (the answer to 7 across) for H, giving REHYCLE, and 'soup' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lechery is excessive sexual desire, so the single word stands as a synonym.

clue.text: Purchaser announced for cowshed

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is taken by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone buying a farm building has it read out.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a farm building where cattle are kept, the same thing as a cowshed.

clue.text: Gorge on nearly all of end product of wheat

parts.note: to gorge is to glut oneself, eat to excess

indicators.note: says the word loses its last letter, leaving almost the whole

explanation.surface: Stuffing oneself on almost all the final output of a wheat field.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat flour, one of the products the grain yields.

clue.text: Magnanimous spirit of Samaritans' opening report

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so the description is spoken and heard as one word

parts.note: the opening of Samaritans is a capital, that is large, S

explanation.surface: The generous spirit of a charity is described in its first account.
explanation.walkthrough: The Samaritans is a British charity. Its opening letter is a capital S, a 'large S', and spoken aloud that phrase gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generosity of spirit, a liberal giving, which matches a magnanimous spirit.

clue.text: Pharmacy's daily record with entry for 'shilling quills'

indicators.note: says the second piece goes into the first

parts.note: a diary is a daily record
S is the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
quills were the pens of old

explanation.surface: A chemist's day book makes room for old money and writing quills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pharmacy's' reads as 'pharmacy is', and the 's is a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensary is a place where medicines are made up and given out, a pharmacy.

clue.text: Lowly Dr Batty devoted to this life and its enjoyments

definitions.text: devoted to this life and its enjoyments

indicators.note: batty means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A humble eccentric doctor is fond of earthly pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' rearranges LOWLY and DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A worldly person is concerned with material, earthly life rather than spiritual matters.

clue.text: Create something different with cold celery soup

indicators.note: a soup mixes its ingredients, so these letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Turn chilled celery into a dish of something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' rearranges C and CELERY.
explanation.definitionFit: To recycle is to convert waste into something new and different.

clue.text: In the Arctic a 'rib' ought to be carved reindeer

indicators.note: says the answer is held within the words that follow, which are 'to be carved' out

explanation.surface: In the Arctic a rib cut from an animal is due for carving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside 'Arctic a rib ought', and 'to be carved' says the answer is cut out of those words.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, the same deer species.

clue.text: Futuristic transport came back in a new version of the Mini

indicators.note: puts one piece inside the other
a new version is a remake, so these letters are rearranged
says the word came is read backwards

explanation.surface: A future model car returned in a redesigned Mini.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came back' gives EMAC, and 'in' puts it inside TIMHINE, which 'a new version of' makes from THE MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: A time machine is the fictional vehicle that carries travellers into the future.

clue.text: Cheaply produced lace?

explanation.surface: Is this lace a low-budget item?
explanation.walkthrough: Something made 'on a shoestring' is produced on very little money.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoestring is a shoelace, and the word also describes a tiny budget.

clue.text: Limit of flying leap

indicators.note: something sent flying is scattered, so the letters go into a new order

explanation.surface: How far a jump in the air can go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges LEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale is a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale', the limit of acceptable conduct.

clue.text: Aura of change embracing sleeveless dress

indicators.note: says the first piece hugs the second inside it

parts.note: small change is pence, the coins in a pocket

indicators.note: without its sleeves, the word dress loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Coins wrapped round a sleeveless frock give off a special air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleeveless' takes the outer letters off the dress, leaving its middle, which 'embracing' tucks inside the coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence is a striking personal quality or air, an aura someone carries.

clue.text: One or two maybe are late

definitions.text: One or two maybe are late

parts.words: One or two maybe are late
parts.note: times like one or two o'clock come late at night, after midnight

explanation.definitionFit: The early morning hours after midnight are times that seem very late at night.

clue.text: 'Road To Hell' — with Rea a gig's nicely raw

indicators.note: letters sent to hell are wrecked and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Chris Rea's song 'The Road to Hell' is played rough at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Rea's song 'The Road to Hell' is often taken to be about the M25 motorway. 'To Hell' rearranges REA A GIGS NICELY RAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A single carriageway is a road with no central reservation, one stretch for both directions.

clue.text: See 14
Rail absurdly against son getting into bizarre country ways

indicators.note: says the pieces go inside another word

parts.note: rum is a British word for odd or bizarre

indicators.note: something done absurdly is muddled, so the letters go into a new order

explanation.surface: Railways oddly at odds with a son going into strange rustic habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurdly' shuffles the rail, and 'getting into' puts that and the son inside the word for bizarre. 'against' just joins the pieces; 'rum' meaning odd is British.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruralism is a rustic way of life, the habits and manners of the countryside.

clue.text: Strike triumphant expression during 'Peace on Earth'

indicators.note: says one piece comes inside the other

parts.note: ole is a cry of triumph, as at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A cheer of victory rings out in the middle of a peace message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts the bullfight cry inside the Latin peace and the Earth; 'on' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To poleaxe is to strike down hard, as with a heavy axe or a blow.

clue.text: Grease protects any rope

indicators.note: a word that protects another wraps around it

parts.note: lard is a cooking fat, a grease

explanation.surface: Lubricant keeps any line safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' means the fat wraps around the word any, as a guard surrounds what it protects.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a short rope or cord, as used on a ship or for a whistle.

clue.text: Car breaker?

explanation.surface: Who smashes cars?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roller' is British slang for a Rolls-Royce, and a long wave that breaks on a shore is a roller.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce car and the name of a big rolling breaking wave.

clue.text: Odd-jobber's hinges tip and many back-to-front

indicators.note: the tip of the word is its first letter
the back letter of the word many is brought round to the front

explanation.surface: A jack-of-all-trades sees to hinge ends and many reversed parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' moves the Y of MANY to the front, giving YMAN. 'Odd-jobber's' reads as 'odd-jobber is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handyman does odd jobs and small repairs around a house, so he is an odd-jobber.

clue.text: Get Man U missing a shot with cheeky trick

indicators.note: shot means ruined, so the letters are thrown into a new order
says a letter is left out of the words before it

explanation.surface: A Manchester United side miss with an audacious bit of skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Man U is Manchester United. 'missing' drops the A, leaving GETMNU, and 'shot' rearranges it. A nutmeg in football is kicking the ball through an opponent's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutmeg is the cheeky football trick of playing the ball between an opponent's legs.

clue.text: Sit-in starts to disrupt every mundane operation

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A protest begins to disrupt every routine operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo, short for demonstration, is a protest, and a sit-in is one kind.

clue.text: Ghastly new craft from stem to stern

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion, so the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A dreadful new boat runs from bow to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat, but it is the verb that rearranges GHASTLY and NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem to stern means along the whole length of a ship, that is in the long direction.

clue.text: Free from impurities? What's the odds?

indicators.note: the odd letters, first, third and so on, of the words are taken

explanation.surface: Why bother cleaning? What does it matter?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the odds?' looks like a shrug, but 'odds' picks the odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something is to clean it and so rid it of dirt.

clue.text: Former wife hacks organ?

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

explanation.surface: An ex-wife chops at a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like a body part, but means a newspaper; the Express is a British daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or publication, and the Express is one such British title.

clue.text: Condemn navy involvement in botched rescue

indicators.note: says one piece is wrapped inside the other
a botched job is messed up, so the letters go into a new order

explanation.surface: Criticise the navy's part in a failed rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges RESCUE, and 'involvement in' puts N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To censure is to criticise formally, to condemn.
